subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift as a core durable run-state contract, and which artifact, timer, persistence, feature-flag, and post-green semantics should that contract enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix chooses public runtime semantics, persisted state ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and config/flag shape across core agent execution.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Existing Lifecycle Surfaces
options.body: Implement only the missing guarantees by extending current loop detection, heartbeat response, task status, subagent lifecycle, and cron watchdog paths without creating a parallel state source.

options.title: Narrow Or Close As Adjacent
options.body: Decide current loop, heartbeat, liveness, and no-fake-progress mitigations are sufficient, then narrow this issue to a smaller reproducible remaining gap or close it by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available routing candidate because the remaining choice is diagnostic/liveness product-contract design rather than a narrow tool-loop patch.
